target_concept: Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes across a project.

mcq.questionText: Which statement correctly explains why Git is classified as a distributed version control system (DVCS)?
options: Git stores a complete copy of the repository on each developer’s machine, allowing independent work and history tracking.
Git requires a central server to store the entire project history, and clients only have a working copy.
Git tracks changes only in binary files and does not record text file modifications.
Git automatically merges changes without any user configuration or conflict resolution.
mcq.correctAnswer: Git stores a complete copy of the repository on each developer’s machine, allowing independent work and history tracking.
mcq.explanation: Git is a DVCS because every clone contains the full repository history, enabling developers to work offline and synchronize changes later. This distributed nature distinguishes it from centralized systems that rely on a single server for history storage.
